name: GitHub
description: Connect GitHub repository access or authenticate GitHub Copilot agents.

methods.whenToUse: Connect your GitHub account for durable MCP, shell Git, gh, and repository access.
methods.guidanceMd: Authorize Paperclip, then choose selected repositories in GitHub. You can edit repository access later from GitHub's installation settings.
methods.label: Connect GitHub
warnings: Shell Git and gh receive this identity for the run and are not constrained by per-tool Ask-first controls.

methods.whenToUse: Use the provider-hosted connection for the quickest setup.
methods.guidanceMd: Create a fine-grained token limited to the repositories agents should use.
methods.label: Personal access token (advanced)

credentialFields.label: GitHub token
credentialFields.helperMd: Repository contents, issues, pull requests and other granted toolsets; selected repos and installation/PAT permissions apply. Create a key with read and write permissions for these actions; Paperclip cannot increase an existing key’s permissions.

methods.label: GitHub Copilot personal access token
methods.whenToUse: Authenticate the GitHub Copilot agent runtime with a personal or explicitly shared account.
methods.guidanceMd: Create a personal fine-grained token with the Copilot Requests permission. Copilot authentication is separate from repository and MCP access. [GitHub authentication instructions](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/set-up-copilot-cli/authenticate-copilot-cli).

credentialFields.label: Personal access token
credentialFields.helperMd: Use a personal fine-grained token with Copilot Requests permission.

methods.label: Custom GitHub App
methods.whenToUse: Use your own GitHub App to give agents a bot identity for GitHub tools, Git and gh.
methods.guidanceMd: Create a GitHub App in your user or organization settings, then install it on the repositories you want to connect. Webhooks and OAuth callbacks are not required. Enter its IDs, repository access and private key below.

tenantFields.label: App ID or Client ID
tenantFields.helperMd: In GitHub, open Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps → your App. Copy the App ID or Client ID from its settings page.

tenantFields.label: Installation ID
tenantFields.helperMd: In your App settings, open Install App, then Configure for the target account. Copy the number after /installations/ in the URL.

tenantFields.label: Repositories
tenantFields.helperMd: Enter owner/repository names separated by commas. Each repository must be included in this App installation.

tenantFields.label: GitHub permissions

options.label: Read: contents, pull requests and issues
Author: write contents and pull requests, read issues
Reviewer: read contents and issues, write pull requests

tenantFields.helperMd: Grant these permissions in the App’s GitHub settings, then approve any changes for its installation. Paperclip cannot grant permissions the installation does not have.

tenantFields.label: Custom permissions (JSON)
tenantFields.helperMd: Use GitHub API permission names with read, write or admin levels, for example: {"contents":"read","checks":"write"}. This replaces the preset; only the permissions you enter are requested.

credentialFields.label: App private key (PEM)
credentialFields.helperMd: In your App’s GitHub settings, under Private keys, choose Generate a private key. Open the downloaded .pem file and paste its entire contents, including the BEGIN and END lines. Paperclip encrypts the saved key.

warnings: Git and gh use this bot’s repository access and GitHub permissions. Paperclip’s per-tool Ask-first controls do not apply to Git or gh.
Existing tokens can remain usable until GitHub expires or revokes them. Use separate Apps for author and reviewer identities.
